# Final review

## Added findings and probe evidence

- **N01 · F after caller-variable reassignment.** F takes the account pointer from its argument during admission, increments that account’s Requests and returns a callback using the saved account pointer. The probe obtains the callback through a local `*Port`, aliases the original Port, and assigns a distinct Port to only the caller variable. Before and after delivery it checks both public Target fields, both epochs and both sets of counters. The original account goes from `(1, 0)` to `(1, 1)`; the incoming account stays at `(0, 0)`. The preserved F target-replacement probes exercise a write to the original Port’s Target field, so their results alone do not establish this ordered sequence. [Source](../component.go#L30) · [Probe](./_postprobe/postreview_test.go#L9)
- **N02 · D with an alias under another key.** After admission at `work`, deletion of `work` makes an invocation return without credit even with the admitted account still reachable at `other`. Reinserting that same account at `work` leaves its counters at `(1, 0)` until the next invocation, which makes them `(1, 1)`. F36–F37 cover deleting the key and later crediting a replacement account. F42 covers an unrelated key pointing to another account. The new sequence covers the admitted account still present under a different key, followed by restoration of the admitted pointer. [Source](../component.go#L22) · [Probe](./_postprobe/postreview_test.go#L37)
- **N03 and N04 · Nil object at admission.** These are source observations. A nil `*Port` passed to F panics evaluating `p.Target` at line 31, before line 32. A nil `*Registry` receiver for D panics evaluating `r.Entries` before the lookup or increment at line 23. F64 and F62 exercise non-nil containers with an unavailable target or entry. The panic helper establishes that a panic occurs for those historical inputs. The precise evaluation sites follow from the source and Go’s nil pointer field selection. [F](../component.go#L31) · [D](../component.go#L23)

## Preserved findings and qualifications

`final.json` contains the 74 original rows in their original order, byte-for-byte through the last original row, with N01–N04 appended. `supplement.json` records 42 qualifications and the two new test bindings. The validator accepted the file shapes, citations, overlay and preservation. The validator checks structure and immutable hashes. The Go assertions and source review establish the behavior. [Findings](./final.json) · [Supplement](./supplement.json) · [Validator](../validate_postreview.py)

- **F07–F18 and F53–F58.** For A, B, C, E and F the replacement operation writes `Target` on the original Port. For D it writes the admission key on the same Registry. The exact replacement counter totals use an incoming account initialized with zero counters. F53–F58 admit twice and explicitly deliver the newer callback before the older one. The older A and D callbacks put a second success on the incoming account, the older C callback adds zero, and the older B, E and F callbacks credit the original. [Replacement seam](./_probe/identity_test.go#L40) · [Replacement assertions](./_probe/identity_test.go#L81) · [Overlapping admissions](./_probe/identity_test.go#L265)
- **F32–F35 and F59–F64.** The cited detached-callback panic assertion is A’s branch. B, C, E and F invoke directly, and C’s identity mismatch short-circuits the epoch check. The admission panic assert for D is at line 298 and the Port assert at line 303. The common panic helper checks the existence of a recovered panic. F31’s nil-target callback panic and later successful invocation remain supported, as do C’s detached no-op and D’s absent, nil-entry and nil-map no-ops after successful admission. [Detach probe](./_probe/identity_test.go#L138) · [Panic helper](./_probe/identity_test.go#L62) · [Invalid admission probe](./_probe/identity_test.go#L285) · [C callback](../component.go#L20)
- **F47–F52.** The first callback is discarded at the first admission, before the second admission. The counter checkpoints follow that order. Only the second callback is invoked, twice, adding one success per call in this sequence. [Probe](./_probe/identity_test.go#L252)
- **F66.** The test writes Requests to zero and writes Successes directly to 10, from its existing zero value. The B callback increments that live field to 11 and leaves Requests at zero. A distinct assignment of zero to Successes was absent from the executed schedule. [Source](../component.go#L15) · [Probe](./_probe/identity_test.go#L324)
- **F67–F72 and F73.** The caller-departure probes model a caller retaining a function and making either zero calls or one later explicit call after replacement. They expose no actual wait or cancellation. F73’s absolute counter observations use two accounts initially at zero. Changing the replacement epoch alone leaves its counters unchanged. An explicit later call credits it once. F74 likewise observes no credit while either check fails and one credit only after pointer and epoch both match at invocation. [Caller-departure probe](./_probe/lifecycle_test.go#L9) · [Mismatch and restoration probe](./_probe/lifecycle_test.go#L41)

The completion-before-change controls F25–F30 deliver first, then change the epoch, detach or delete, and install a replacement with no further invocation. Their credited result persists through those writes. The restoration probes likewise require explicit invocation for any later credit. The history in F31–F46 and F73–F74 supports re-evaluation on each call, including after a skipped call and, for A, after a recovered panic. [Completion before change](./_probe/identity_test.go#L118) · [Restoration](./_probe/identity_test.go#L222)

# Final review summary

- Retained all 74 baseline findings, including their wording, order and open questions. Added four findings and recorded 42 qualifications covering test scope, setup conditions, exact ordering and citation precision. [Findings](./final.json) · [Supplement](./supplement.json)
- F’s saved callback credited the original account after only the caller’s local `*Port` variable was reassigned. Both Port targets and account epochs stayed as expected, and the new account’s counters stayed at zero. D skipped credit while its saved key was absent even though another key still pointed to the account. It credited the account on explicit delivery after key restoration. [New probes](./_postprobe/postreview_test.go)
- The race-enabled overlay run passed all 21 top-level tests and their subtests on each of three repetitions, with zero skips or failures. The preservation validator passed. [Go log](../../logs/026.stdout) · [Validator log](../../logs/057.stdout)
- The nil `*Port` and nil `*Registry` admission findings are source observations. The review explains why those two claims and B’s observed counter-reset behavior stand despite unclear Jev verdicts. All lifecycle intent questions remain open. [Review](./review.md) · [Original questions](../baseline/open-questions.md)
